description: A projected demand in a region: an exogenous load profile that must be served, with optional voluntary curtailment and time shifting. A demand with existing loads in the base system takes its peak from them and grows from the base year; a new demand starts in its construction year at `peak_demand_mw`. Conforming demands grow by `growth_rate`. Curtailment up to `max_demand_curtailment` is priced by `curtailment_cost`, and the rest of the demand by `value_of_lost_load`.

available.description: Indicator of whether the component is connected and online (`true`) or disconnected, offline, or down (`false`).

power_systems_type.description: Corresponding type to be used in PCM modeling.

region.description: Location where the component applies. Can be a zone or node.

peak_demand_mw.description: Peak demand. Demands with existing loads in the base system derive their peak demand from those loads, not from this value. Units: MW.

construction_year.description: The year in which a new demand starts. Should only be used for new demands.

growth_rate.description: The annual growth rate of the demand, used to scale present-day loads into future projections. Only used for conforming demands. Units: 1.

conformity.description: Whether the demand is conforming (grows by `growth_rate`) or non-conforming (does not grow). Must be set for new demands.

max_demand_curtailment.description: Maximum fraction of demand that can be curtailed voluntarily. Units: 1.

curtailment_cost.description: Cost of voluntary curtailment. A linear curve is a single price for all curtailable demand; a piecewise incremental curve gives tiers whose x coordinates are fractions of demand, from 0 to `max_demand_curtailment`, and whose slopes are prices. Units: USD/MWh.

value_of_lost_load.description: Cost of involuntary shedding of the demand that cannot be curtailed. Units: USD/MWh.

flexible_fraction.description: Fraction of demand that can be shifted in time. Units: 1.

max_demand_delay.description: Maximum time that flexible demand can be delayed. Units: min.

max_demand_advance.description: Maximum time that flexible demand can be served in advance. Units: min.

shift_efficiency.description: Fraction of shifted energy that is kept. Represents energy losses due to time shifting. Units: 1.

shift_cost.description: Cost of shifting demand, per MWh shifted. Units: USD/MWh.

title: ProjectedDemand
